title: Quantifying covariate effects on the kinetics of ethanol
summary:
In this clinical study, various factors influencing the distribution and the metabolism of ethanol (ethyl alcohol, often just described as alcohol) in the human body will be studied, which subsequently may determine the time course of alcohol concentrations in blood. 
The influencing factors examined include various personal data (age, ethnicity, body weight, sex, body height) in combination with characteristics of the genetic material. In addition, it will be studied whether metabolites produced naturally in the body are related to distribution and metabolism of ethanol. 
The study has the greater objective to develop a better model of the metabolism of alcohol and thus – based on the model and the influencing factors evaluated – to improve the prediction of respective blood alcohol concentrations for a given consumption.
conditions: The objectives of this trial are not related in any way to assess safety or efficacy of intravenous or oral ethanol, it aims to develop a pharmacokinetic model to assess inter-individual variability.

interventions.name: Patients with high oral administration rate of ethanol with a bolus dose of 0.7g/kg BW (0.35g/kg BW in Asians and patients older than 65 years respectively)

Patients with low oral administration rate of ethanol with a bolus dose of 0.7g/kg BW (0.35g/kg BW in Asians and patients older than 65 years respectively); 7 fractions will be taken in 10 min intervals

Patients with intravenous administration of ethanol with an infusion of 0.5g/kg BW (0.25g/kg BW in Asians respectively); 50 g ethanol (Alkohol-Konzentrat 95 % Braun) will be dissolved in 1L 5% glucose solution and the appropriate volume is administered over 1 hour
